mc.q:
A computer receives the three data sequences, shown below. Each sequence includes a parity bit. Two of the sequences are found to be corrupted during transmission.
First:  0101 0111
Second: 1101 0101
Third:  1110 1011
Which of the following best describes the situation?
o: Corrupted data sequence: The first and second, Parity check: Even
Corrupted data sequence: The second and third, Parity check: Even
Corrupted data sequence: The first and second, Parity check: Odd
Corrupted data sequence: The second and third, Parity check: Odd
mc.exp: Count the 1s: first has 5, second 5, third 6. Two sequences are odd and one is even. If even parity was used, the first and second (odd count) are corrupted.

mc.q:
A supermarket uses a database table FRUIT, which stores fruit name FNAME and the corresponding quantity in stock QTY. Which of the following best describes the result of the query below?
SELECT FNAME
FROM FRUIT
WHERE QTY > 0
ORDER BY QTY DESC
o: Fruits are listed in descending order of fruit name.
Fruits are listed in ascending order of the quantity in stock.
Fruits with low quantities in stock are listed in ascending order of fruit name.
Fruits are listed in descending order of the quantity in stock.
mc.exp: ORDER BY QTY DESC sorts by quantity, highest first. Only fruits in stock (QTY > 0) appear.

mc.q:
What are the advantages of using the following calendar box over a text box for entering a date?
[Calendar box: April 2021]
st: Avoids impossible dates.
Ensures that the input is error-free.
Provides a user-friendly interface.
mc.exp: A calendar stops impossible dates and is easy to use, but the user can still click the wrong date, so input is not error-free.

mc.q: Which of the following additions of 4-bit numbers using two's complement representation will result in an overflow error?
mc.exp: C: 1100 = −4, 1011 = −5, sum −9 is below −8. Two negatives give 0111 (positive), so overflow.

mc.q: How many bits are required to represent an image of 8×8 black-and-white pixels?
mc.exp: Black-and-white needs 1 bit per pixel: 8 × 8 × 1 = 64 bits.

mc.q: Which of the following is correct?
o: Information process: Data collection, Example: Creating a statistical chart
Information process: Data preparation, Example: Validating questionnaires before input
Information process: Data processing, Example: Sorting questionnaires for data entry
Information process: Data organisation, Example: Designing an online questionnaire
mc.exp: Checking questionnaires before input is data preparation. Charts are presentation, designing a form is collection.

mc.q: For a photo, the file size of its BMP image is larger than that of its JPG image because ________.
st: the BMP image is uncompressed
BMP represents a bitmap image
the BMP image cannot be shown in a browser
mc.exp: BMP stores pixels without compression. JPG is also a bitmap, so (2) is not the reason.

mc.q: Which of the following about mail merge are correct?
st: A database file can be used as the data source for mail merge.
A main document and a data source can be merged to produce a merged document.
The content of merge fields is inserted in the merged document when the merging completes.
mc.exp: All three describe how mail merge works.

mc.q: Which of the following about a presentation of several slides supplemented with verbal annotation in presentation software is correct?
o: The presentation should be in a video file format such as MP4.
Verbal annotation can be recorded for slides individually.
The duration of each slide for verbal annotation is the same.
mc.exp: Narration is recorded slide by slide, and each slide can last a different time.

mc.q:
In the following spreadsheet, a formula is entered in B6 based on B2:B4 to calculate the class fee. Classmates want to limit the class fee to $1,000 by cutting the budget for the study tour.
AB
1Expenditure for S6 (30 classmates)$
2Reference books6,000
3Photocopy fee900
4Budget for the study tour30,000
5
6Class fee per classmate1,230
When using the 'goal seek' function for 'what-if' analysis, which of the following sets of data should be used?
o: Set cell: $B$4, To value: 1000, By changing cell: $B$6
Set cell: $B$4, To value: 30000, By changing cell: $B$6
Set cell: $B$6, To value: 1000, By changing cell: $B$4
Set cell: $B$6, To value: 30000, By changing cell: $B$4
mc.exp: Set the result cell (fee, B6) to the target 1000 by changing the input (tour budget, B4).

mc.q: Why should characters be represented by character sets such as ASCII in computers?
st: To standardise the data representation
To enhance the data encryption
As data in computers is stored in binary numbers
mc.exp: Character sets give every character a standard binary code. They have nothing to do with encryption.

mc.q: Why is information literacy important in a knowledge-based society?
st: People should be able to identify fake information and hoaxes on the Internet.
People should be able to write artificial intelligence (AI) programs.
People should understand that some information from the Internet lacks credibility.
mc.exp: Information literacy is judging information. Writing AI programs is not part of it.

mc.q: When developing a management information system, which of the following should be the first item to be considered?
mc.exp: You first need to know what the system is for. Technology, people and cost follow from that.

mc.q: Which of the following is/are the common specification(s) of a home use printer?
st: Parallel port
1200 dpi
mc.exp: Home printers have Wi-Fi (802.11n) and a resolution like 1200 dpi. Parallel ports are obsolete.

mc.q: A standalone computer runs slow when working on database software. Which of the following hardware components should be upgraded?
st: RAM
ROM
Network interface card
mc.exp: More RAM helps. ROM is not upgraded for speed, and a standalone computer does not use the network.

mc.q: Why would a fast food shop install a thermal printer instead of a laser printer to print receipts at the cashier?
st: The printout is black and white.
The printer is smaller in size.
The text on the printout will fade faster.
mc.exp: A thermal printer is small, which suits a cashier. Laser printers can also print black and white, and fading is a drawback, not a reason.

mc.q: One day, Mary finds that she cannot access the Internet through her computer at home. Which of the following is a possible cause?
o: The size of ROM is small.
The data transfer rate of the hard disk is low.
The graphics card is out of order.
The network interface card is out of order.
mc.exp: The network interface card connects the computer to the network. The others do not stop Internet access.

mc.q: Why do we need to regularly update software?
st: Fix program bugs.
Provide new functions.
Improve the software performance.
mc.exp: Updates fix bugs, add functions and improve performance: all three.

mc.q: A company develops a computer system for autopilot driving, so that a vehicle can collect and use image data from the environment and drive on the road safely. It is a real-time processing system because ________.
o: the computers involved should have a high processing power
there should be no time delay between data input and the data processing
a large amount of data should be collected over a period of time
it provides resources and services to multiple users at a time
mc.exp: Real-time means input is processed immediately. C describes batch processing and D describes time-sharing.

mc.q: There are one hundred 300GB surveillance video files. Without any file reorganisation and compression, how many 2TB hard disks are needed to store all the video files?
mc.exp: Files cannot be split. A 2TB (2048GB) disk holds 6 files (1800GB). 100 ÷ 6 = 16.7, so 17 disks.

mc.q:
In a typical situation, what are P, Q and R?
[Diagram: Users ↔ Computer; inside the computer, P is the outer layer, Q is inside P, and R is inside Q]
o: P: Operating system, Q: Hardware, R: Application software
P: Application software, Q: Operating system, R: Hardware
P: Application software, Q: Hardware, R: Operating system
P: Operating system, Q: Application software, R: Hardware
mc.exp: Users talk to application software, which runs on the operating system, which controls the hardware at the core.

mc.q: Which of the following describe(s) the URL, https://www.abc.edu.hk/en/ ?
st: en is a path on the web server.
The domain name is abc.
The web site is registered as an educational institution in Hong Kong.
mc.exp: /en/ is a path, and .edu.hk means a Hong Kong education site. The domain name is www.abc.edu.hk, not just abc.

mc.q: Which of the following are the potential benefits of e-learning?
st: It can track individual learning progress.
It reduces computer hardware resources.
It provides flexible learning schedules.
mc.exp: E-learning tracks progress and lets people learn any time. It needs more hardware, not less.

mc.q: Which of the following should be considered when designing web pages?
st: The time for loading web pages
The user-friendliness of browsing
The colour combination
mc.exp: Loading time, ease of use and colours all matter in web design.

mc.q: Fibre optics is used in a computer network because ________.
st: it supports both wired and wireless connections
its data transfer rate is very high
it supports a connection with a long distance
mc.exp: Fibre is fast and works over long distances. It is a wired medium only.

mc.q: Internet Protocol (IP) is used in a computer network because ________.
o: data can be transmitted under the same communication rules
computers in the network are installed with the same operating system
the maximum data transfer rates between computers are the same
the network is a LAN instead of a WAN
mc.exp: A protocol is a set of shared communication rules, so different machines can talk.

mc.q: Amy uses a computer to watch streaming videos. Which of the following should she consider?
st: Network bandwidth
Anti-virus software
Hard disk storage size
mc.exp: Streaming needs enough bandwidth. The video is not saved, so disk size does not matter.

mc.q:
The final values of X and Y in the following two algorithms are the same:
Algorithm 1
X ← 10
Y ← 0
REPEAT
    X ← X + 1
    Y ← Y + 2
UNTIL (X = 20) OR (Y > 15)

Algorithm 2
X ← 10
Y ← 0
WHILE [Missing part] DO
    X ← X + 1
    Y ← Y + 2
What is the missing part in Algorithm 2?
mc.exp: WHILE needs the opposite of the UNTIL condition. NOT(A OR B) = (NOT A) AND (NOT B): (X <> 20) AND (Y <= 15).

mc.q:
What input value for the algorithm below will not output 'Complete!'?
Input N
flag ← TRUE
While flag = TRUE do
     If remainder of (N/4) > 0 then
          flag ← FALSE
Output 'Complete!'
mc.exp: For N = 4 the remainder is 0, so flag never becomes FALSE and the loop runs forever.

mc.q:
Answer Questions 30 and 31 with reference to the following algorithm.
j ← 0
Input N
While N <> 888 do
    j ← j + N
    Input N
Output j

What is the purpose of the algorithm?
o: Counts the number of input values.
Calculates the sum of input values.
Calculates the average of input values.
mc.exp: j ← j + N adds each input to a running total: the sum.

mc.q:
(Refer to the algorithm in Question 30.)
j ← 0
Input N
While N <> 888 do
    j ← j + N
    Input N
Output j

What is the use of the value '888'?
o: Limits the range of input values.
mc.exp: 888 is a sentinel (rogue) value: entering it ends the loop.

mc.q: What is the importance of a problem definition in problem-solving?
o: The design and the scope of work can be set.
There is no need to define sub-problems.
An error-free algorithm will be developed.
mc.exp: Defining the problem sets the scope of the work. It never removes later steps or guarantees no errors.

mc.q: Which of the following is/are the advantage(s) of modularity in programming?
st: The user manual is simpler.
It is easier to trace a program.
It facilitates programming through team work.
mc.exp: Modules are easier to trace and can be shared among a team. Users never see the modules, so the manual is not affected.

mc.q: Why should appropriate test data be prepared?
st: To detect mistakes in algorithms
To test whether exceptional input data can be handled
To verify expected results from given input data
mc.exp: Test data finds errors, checks exceptional cases and compares output with expected results: all three.

mc.q: Peter just finds that he cannot open some important files in a computer in his office due to a ransomware attack. What should he do immediately?
mc.exp: Disconnect first so the ransomware cannot spread to other computers on the network.

mc.q: A shopping mall plans to develop a mobile application for customers to register their shopping records and gain bonus points for gifts. Which of the following considerations should be the least important?
mc.exp: Security, privacy and which OS to support all matter. App file size matters least.

mc.q: John plays Internet games and uses social media all the time. Which of the following are likely the consequences of such indulgence in Internet activities?
st: A higher chance of having anxiety and attention problems
Infringement of copyright in Internet activities
A decline in physical fitness
mc.exp: Too much screen time harms mental health and fitness. Heavy use does not by itself mean copyright infringement.

mc.q: Which of the following are appropriate when using a social media application?
st: Understand the terms of use of the application.
Provide necessary personal information only.
Forward information sent from others to friends as soon as possible.
mc.exp: Read the terms and share as little personal data as possible. Forwarding without checking spreads rumours.

mc.q: Peter installs a software package on his computer. He also installs it on another computer. He does not infringe copyright because ________.
st: the license of the software package allows such installation
the two computers are located in different countries
the operating systems of the two computers are different
mc.exp: Only the licence decides whether a second installation is allowed.

mc.q: Which of the following about the use of robots are correct?
st: Robots can follow working procedures accurately.
Robots can replace the work of all the employees.
Robots can take up dirty, dangerous jobs.
mc.exp: Robots are accurate and can do dirty or dangerous work, but they cannot replace every employee.

lq.stem: Peter decides to buy a computer with a quad-core CPU instead of a dual-core CPU.

parts.q: Why does Peter make this decision?
parts.ms: It can execute instructions faster (shorter processing time). / It has more computational power. / It performs more tasks simultaneously (distribute the workload) (1)

parts.q: Suggest another CPU technical specification that he might consider.
parts.ms: Clock rate / word length (word size) (1)

parts.q: Peter will use his computer to edit and render videos. Give two hardware components that he should consider, other than the CPU. Explain briefly.
parts.ms:
RAM / Hard disk (SSD) / GPU with a simple but reasonable explanation (1 × 2)
Suggested answer: More RAM, so large video files and editing software can be held in memory without slowing down; a dedicated GPU, which speeds up rendering and video effects.

parts.q: Peter buys a new computer with a pre-installed operating system. List two common functions of the operating system, other than file management.
parts.ms: Any two (1 × 2): Process management / resource management (memory management / network management / device management) / user interface

parts.q: He uses free cloud storage for storing video files. Give an advantage and a disadvantage of using the cloud storage over a portable hard disk.
parts.ms:
Advantage (1): File sharing is simpler / Files can be accessed anywhere without bringing the hard disk. / It can be simultaneously accessed by different devices. / Accessible regardless of OS / It can be available free-of-charge / Easy upgrade
Disadvantage (1): The access time is longer. / Require Internet access.

parts.q: Peter considers installing open source software and freeware. State two differences between them.
parts.ms:
Source code in open source software can be seen / modified / redistributed. (1 × 2)
Suggested answer: Open source software provides its source code, but freeware usually does not; users may modify and redistribute open source software, but freeware cannot be modified (and its redistribution may be restricted by the developer).

parts.q:
When Peter installs application software, the following dialogue box is shown:
Terms of service
Before installing this application software, you must read and accept the terms of service below:
1. This agreement governs your use of this service.
2. …
⋮
☐ I agree to the terms of service.
Give a term of service regarding privacy. Describe the potential risk of accepting this term that Peter might encounter.
parts.ms:
Example of terms of service (1): Accept the use of the contact list or photos in users' devices. (Accessing resources [hardware / function / files] of the devices) / Collect personal information from the users / Collect daily information about the use of the software / Allow to use personal information (Information collection)
Potential risk, echoing the term of service stated above (1): Personal information is leaked (info leakage) / Receive unwanted advertisement / spam (spamming)

lq.stem:
A spreadsheet file with two worksheets, Sheet1 and Sheet2, are used for processing an inter-house singing contest. In Sheet1, Column A stores the house code (HCODE) and Column B stores the names of houses (HOUSE). Part of the data is shown below:
Sheet1
AB
1HCODEHOUSE
2RRed
3YYellow
4BBlue
5GGreen
Sheet2
ABCDEFG
1HCODEHOUSEParticipant_CodeScore_1Score_2Score_3FS
2B0180808080
3Y0296949295
4R0360646464
5G0480808080
6G0570809085
7B0675756975
8G0760686868

parts.q: In Sheet2, the final score FS is the average of the highest two scores from the three scores in columns D to F. A formula in G2 is copied to G3:G8. Write down the formula in G2.
parts.ms:
=(sum($D2:$F2)-min($D2:$F2))/2 (1 + 1)
Alternatives:
=(large($D2:$F2,2) + max($D2:$F2))/2
=(large($D2:$F2,2) + large($D2:$F2,1))/2
=(small($D2:$F2,2) + small($D2:$F2,3))/2
=average(large($D2:$F2,2),max($D2:$F2))
(1) Functions to find out the max and the second max
(1) all correct

parts.q:
In Sheet2, a formula =vlookup(A2, Sheet1!A2:B5, 2, false) is entered in B2 and then copied to B3:B8. It is found that not the names of all houses are correctly shown. Write down the correct formula in B2.
=vlookup( ___ , ___ , ___ , ___ )
parts.ms:
=vlookup($A2, Sheet1!$A$2:$B$5, 2, false) (1 + 1)
(1) Correct absolute / mixed address for the range A2:B5
(1) all correct

parts.q:
In Sheet2, a pivot chart is created for displaying the number of participants in each house.
[Bar chart: Blue, Yellow, Red, Green]
Complete the following parts to create the pivot chart.
ROWS: ______ VALUES: ______
parts.ms:
ROWS: HOUSE / Column B (1)
VALUES: Count of HOUSE / Count of HCODE (other reasonable answer) (1)

parts.q: The pivot chart can be inserted into a document using two methods, linking and embedding. Give an advantage of each method.
parts.ms:
Linking: The content is automatically updated whenever a change occurs in the linked chart. / The file size of the document will not increase drastically. (1)
Embedding: There is only one file to manage. (1)

parts.q: Sheet2 is converted to a database table TB2. Suggest a primary key for TB2 : ______
parts.ms: Participant_Code / Column C

parts.q:
Based on the given data in Sheet2, what is the output after executing the following SQL statement? 
SELECT HCODE, MAX(FS) FROM TB2 GROUP BY HCODE
parts.ms:
B 80
Y 95
R 64
G 85
(1) GROUP BY (4 rows with correct HCODE)
(1) Maximum (correct calculation) + others (column order, no extra fields/symbols)
* The row order is not significant.

parts.q: Would you suggest using a spreadsheet or database to process the data of the singing contest? Explain briefly.
parts.ms:
Database: generate reports / query / data validation OR Spreadsheet: create charts / small data size (1)
* No mark without mentioning database or spreadsheet

lq.stem:
A school designs the following computer network. P and Q are common network connecting devices. A computer X connects to P. Some tablets connect to Q.
[Diagram: Internet — Router (wired), Web server — Router (wired), Router — P — Q (wired), X — P (wired), Q ))) Tablets (WiFi), Z — Internet (wired)]

parts.q:
What are P and Q?
P: ______ Q: ______
parts.ms:
P: switch / hub (1)
Q: AP / (wireless) Access Point / wireless router (1)

parts.q: What is the main function of the router in the network?
parts.ms: Route network packets based on their IP addresses to other networks or devices. / Manage traffic between networks. / Connect different networks / connect LAN to WAN (1)

parts.q:
Computer X sends a file to a computer Z. Complete the following steps to describe how data is transmitted.
1. The file ______.
2. The packets are sent out from X.
3. The packets ______.
4. The completion of the transmission of all the packets is ensured.
5. The packets ______.
parts.ms:
1. The file are broken into packets (1)
3. The packets are transmitted through the Internet via different routes (1)
5. The packets are reassembled at Z (1)

parts.q: Is it a must to install a DNS in the school in order that the web server can be accessed by the public? Explain briefly.
parts.ms: No, the public can access the web server using its IP address directly. / the public can access a DNS in another place (ISP). (2*)

parts.q: Give two reasons why a firewall is enabled in X.
parts.ms:
Any two (1 × 2): Permit or block data packets based on a set of security rules / Filter intruders / block unauthorized access / prevent hacking / prevent spyware / ransomware attack / prevent information leakage / log user activity
✗ prevent virus
✗ content filtering

parts.q: The school plans to set up an e-payment system. Other than security tokens, suggest two methods of making secure electronic transactions.
parts.ms:
Any two (1 × 2): SSL encryption, two-factor authentication, biometric authentication, one-time password via SMS/email, smartcard, adopt digital certificates / use a private key to verify the user identity
✗ set login name and password
✗ use a stronger password
✗ change password regularly
✗ show last logon time
✗ validate personal information / identity or enhance server security without further elaboration or illustrating examples

lq.stem: John develops an Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbot application to chat with online users and answer ICT questions.

parts.q:
A dialogue between the chatbot and an online user is shown in the following example:
Chatbot: Hello, I'm a chatbot. How can I help you?
User: Can you tell me a major difference between MP4 and AVI?
According to the dialogue, suggest an answer for the chatbot to reply.
parts.ms: The file size of AVI is larger. / The quality of AVI is better. / MP4 supports streaming. / MP4 supports subtitle/menu. / HTML5 supports MP4 only. / More portable devices/operating systems support MP4. (1)

parts.q: Suggest an improvement to the application for visually impaired people.
parts.ms: Audio input / Text to speech / text size / color contrast (1)

parts.q: Give two ways in which chatbots can influence society.
parts.ms: Any two (1 × 2): Lower the human effort to reply questions. / Provide 7×24 service. / Generate faster responses. / Generate fewer job opportunities.

parts.q:
John develops the login page for using the chatbot application.
[Login page: Username, Password, Captcha (with a distorted-text image), Login and Cancel buttons]
Users should set a password of at least 8 characters that must include an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a symbol. Give two good practices for users when setting a password, other than having a long password.
parts.ms: Any two (1 × 2): Use meaningless words. / Use randomised numbers. / Use different passwords for different systems.

parts.q: How can Captcha enhance the security of the login page?
parts.ms: Users need to read and input the characters that a software bot cannot do. (1)

parts.q:
John considers encoding symbols into bit patterns in the application. The following table shows the bit patterns of symbols using two different methods.
SymbolBit pattern: Method 1Bit pattern: Method 2
😊101
🙃0101
😐00000
☹11001
Encode 😊 😐 ☹ ☹ using Method 1: ______
Decode '001011' using Method 2: ______

Find the number of bits required for encoding the symbols in each row below.
Method 1Method 2
😊 😊 😊 ☹ ☹ ☹
☹ ☹ ☹ 😐 😐 😐
parts.ms:
😊😊😊☹☹☹: Method 1 = 12, Method 2 = 12
☹☹☹😐😐😐: Method 1 = 12, Method 2 = 18 (2)

parts.q: Under what scenario will Method 2 be better than Method 1?
parts.ms: The message contains more 😊. (1)

lq.stem:
Mary designs a subprogram with an array A. She considers algorithms ALG1, ALG2 and ALG3.
ALG1 
Line  Content
1     B ← 0
2     for i from 1 to N do
3         if A[i] = 1 then
4             B ← B + 1
5     if B >= N/2 then
6         ch ← 'X'
7     else
8         ch ← 'Y'

parts.q:
Suppose that N = 6. Execute ALG1 with the following initial content of A:
A[1]A[2]A[3]A[4]A[5]A[6]
101000
Write down the final values of B and ch.
B: ______ ch: ______

Suppose that N = 6. Execute ALG1 with the following initial content of A:
A[1]A[2]A[3]A[4]A[5]A[6]
111100
How many times will Line 3 be executed? ______

ALG2 
Line  Content
1     i ← 1
2     B ← 0
3     while (i <= N) AND (B < N/2) do
4         if A[i] = 1 then
5             B ← B + 1
6         i ← i + 1
7     if B >= N/2 then
8         ch ← 'X'
9     else
10        ch ← 'Y'
Suppose that N = 6. Execute ALG2 with the initial content of A:
A[1]A[2]A[3]A[4]A[5]A[6]
111100
How many times will Line 4 be executed? ______
ALG2 can be more efficient than ALG1. Why?
parts.ms: ALG2 is more efficient as the number of comparisons / executions with the conditional statement on Line 3 is fewer. (1)

parts.q:
Complete the following initial content of A such that the number of executions of the statement 'if A[i] = 1 then' in both ALG1 and ALG2 would be the same.
A[1]A[2]A[3]A[4]A[5]A[6]
11

ALG1 and ALG3 below should always produce the same result. Complete Line 3 below.
ALG3 
Line  Content
1     B ← 0
2     for i from 1 to N do
3         B ← B + A [ ______ ]
4     if B >= N/2 then
5         ch ← 'X'
6     else
7         ch ← 'Y'
parts.ms: i

parts.q: The value of N is very large. Which algorithm, ALG1 or ALG3, is more efficient? Explain briefly.
parts.ms: ALG3. Fewer instructions have to be executed as the conditional statement "if A[i] = 1 then" is removed. (2*)

parts.q: A computer executes Mary's subprogram. State two components in the CPU that are involved in the fetch-decode-execute cycle, other than IR (instruction register).
parts.ms: Any two (1 × 2): MDR (memory data register) / MAR (memory address register) / PC (program counter) / ALU (arithmetic logic unit) / CU (control unit) / SR (status register)
